item.text:
**4B.10 Research Note (Bongbong Marcos, 2024)**

Working read: **slightly stronger than inherited, but only marginally**. Compared with the Duterte baseline, Marcos in 2024 looked more media-friendly, expanded connectivity, and took some accountability steps. But the core coercive patterns inherited from the previous era, especially red-tagging, blocked sites, and pressure on critics, were still in place. I did not find evidence of a major democratic rebound.

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Philippines: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/philippines/freedom-world/2024 | Freedom House says violence and impunity had decreased somewhat since the new administration took office in 2022, but red-tagging and other harmful practices persisted. This is the clearest source for “slightly stronger than inherited, but only modestly.” | 4B.10, 4B.3, 4B.5, 4B.6, 4B.7 |
| Philippines: Freedom on the Net 2024 Country Report | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/philippines/freedom-net/2024 | The report says 26 of 27 Duterte-era blocked sites were still blocked and notes brief mobile-network restrictions in late 2023 and January 2024. That shows inherited digital restrictions were not fully reversed. | 4B.10, 4B.9, 4B.6 |
| Philippines | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | June 17, 2024 | https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/philippines | Reuters Institute said Marcos was more media-friendly than Duterte, but red-tagging, libel pressure, blocked sites, and threats to journalists persisted. This supports a small improvement over inheritance, not a clean democratization. | 4B.10, 4B.3, 4B.6, 4B.9 |
| Red-tagging puts activists at risk | Human Rights Watch | January 11, 2024 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/philippines-red-tagging-puts-activists-risk | HRW says government supporters and officials continued red-tagging critics under Marcos, putting leftist activists at serious risk. This is strong evidence that the inherited coercive environment remained intact. | 4B.10, 4B.3, 4B.5, 4B.6, 4B.7, 4B.9 |
| Dangerous red-tagging of labor leaders | Human Rights Watch | September 25, 2024 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/09/25/philippines-dangerous-red-tagging-labor-leaders | HRW reported officials and security actors threatened union leaders and targeted women’s groups, Indigenous peoples, journalists, teachers, and judges. That argues the democratic field was still substantially constrained. | 4B.10, 4B.3, 4B.5, 4B.6, 4B.7, 4B.9 |
| PBBM ushers Filipinos to a better, brighter, more connected Bagong Pilipinas with the Philippine Domestic Submarine Cable Network launch | Presidential Communications Office | February 15, 2024 | https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-ushers-filipinos-to-a-better-brighter-more-connected-bagong-pilipinas-with-the-philippine-domestic-submarine-cable-network-launch/ | Marcos framed major connectivity expansion as a governance priority, which supports broader information access rather than political closure. That is a small resilience gain. | 4B.10, 4B.6, 4B.9 |
| PBBM orders connectivity in remote, isolated communities | Presidential Communications Office | September 9, 2024 | https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-orders-connectivity-in-remote-isolated-communities/ | The administration pushed free Wi-Fi and connectivity into remote communities. This is modestly pro-democracy because it lowers access barriers, though it is not a direct anti-repression reform. | 4B.10, 4B.6, 4B.9, 4B.7 |
| Govt vows legal action vs deep fake video creators, spreaders | Presidential Communications Office | April 26, 2024 | https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/govt-vows-legal-action-vs-deep-fake-video-creators-spreaders/ | The government treated deepfake manipulation as a legal/institutional problem, not a broad censorship emergency. That helps resilience a bit, but it is defensive rather than transformative. | 4B.10, 4B.6, 4B.9, 4B.5 |
| PCO to designate fact-check officers in state media to fight fake news | Presidential Communications Office | September 9, 2024 | https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pco-to-designate-fact-check-officers-in-state-media-to-fight-fake-news/ | A formal anti-disinformation step inside state media suggests some institutional cleanup, but it does not show independent media or opposition space became safer. | 4B.10, 4B.6, 4B.9, 4B.5 |
| DOJ creates task force to investigate Duterte-era EJKs | Philippine News Agency | November 6, 2024 | https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1237266 | The DOJ task force to investigate prior killings is a real accountability move. That slightly strengthens democratic resilience, though it remains executive-led and incomplete. | 4B.10, 4B.4, 4B.5, 3B.10 |
| Marcos on critics: let Comelec do their job | GMA News Online | January 23, 2024 | https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/topstories/nation/895067/marcos-on-people-s-initiative-for-cha-cha-let-comelec-do-their-job/story/ | Marcos deferred to the election commission on allegations about the people’s initiative drive. This is a small but real sign of procedural restraint rather than executive capture. | 4B.10, 4B.4, 4B.8, 4B.5 |

**Bottom line:** 2024 looks **slightly stronger than the Duterte inheritance**, mostly because Marcos did not replicate the most extreme overt abuses and did make some connectivity, due-process, and accountability moves. But the improvement was **narrow**: red-tagging, blocked sites, and intimidation persisted, so democratic resilience was still fragile rather than robust.

**Search gap:** I did **not** find evidence of a large, year-defining democratic breakthrough in 2024, nor of a full reversal of inherited coercive practices.
